translation_layer.student_language: Skip, together, holding hands, 3 and 4, 7 and 8
translation_layer.teacher_language: Whole step and half step recognition inside the major scale pattern

child.story_hook: Some numbers skip over a neighbor. Some numbers hold hands. In the C family, 3 and 4 hold hands. 7 and 8 hold hands.
child.tone: Warm, concrete, and playful. Use holding hands language freely.

teen.story_hook: The pattern has two moves: skip and together. Most numbers skip. 3 and 4 are together. 7 and 8 are together.
teen.tone: Direct, clear, peer-level. No baby language. Holding hands can appear as the protected Motesart term.

adult.story_hook: The major scale pattern is built from two distances. First learn them as skip and together. The music-world names come after you own the sound.
adult.tone: Efficient and precise. Motesart words first, technical vocabulary earned later.

motesart_intro.child: You already found home. Now we learn how the family moves. Some numbers skip. Some numbers are together. Together means they are holding hands.
motesart_intro.teen: You found home. Now we map the moves. Skip means there is a note between. Together means no note between.
motesart_intro.adult: Home is locked. Now we define the two distances in the pattern: skip and together. Use the relationship first; the technical names come after ownership.

teach.core_concept: Skip means there is a note between. Together means they are right next to each other — no note between them.
teach.motesart_shorthand: 3 and 4 are together. 7 and 8 are together. They are holding hands. Every other pair has a note between them — that is a skip.
key_facts: Skip means there is a note between.
Every other pair in the major scale pattern is a skip.

motesart_language.skip_definition: Skip means there is one note between the two numbers.
motesart_language.together_definition: Together means the two numbers are right next to each other with no note between.

teach.visual_aid: skip vs together diagram — wide gap vs no gap

step_1_story_hook.name: Story Hook
step_1_story_hook.child: Every family has ways it moves. Some numbers skip over a neighbor. Some numbers stay together and hold hands. In this gate, we find both.
step_1_story_hook.teen: The pattern has two moves: skip and together. Once you see those two moves, the whole scale starts making sense.
step_1_story_hook.adult: This gate separates the two distances in the major scale pattern. We will call them skip and together first.
step_1_story_hook.visual: Eight numbered scale positions appear. 3 and 4 glow together. 7 and 8 glow together. The other pairs show a small space.
step_1_story_hook.audio: play adjacent pairs for together and spaced pairs for skip

step_2_hear_it.name: Hear It
step_2_hear_it.description: Student hears skip and together before technical names are introduced.
step_2_hear_it.motesart_intro: Listen first. This one has space — that is skip. This one is right next door — that is together. 3 and 4 are together. 7 and 8 are together.
step_2_hear_it.visual: Number pairs light up as the audio plays. 3-4 and 7-8 show no gap.

step_3_say_it.name: Say It
step_3_say_it.description: Call and response. Motesart words only.

rounds.motesart_prompt: When there is a note between, we call it...
rounds.motesart_wrong: That move is a skip. Say it back: skip.

rounds.motesart_prompt: When two numbers are right next to each other, we call it...
rounds.motesart_wrong: That move is together. No note between.

acceptable_answers: three and four and seven and eight
rounds.motesart_wrong: The together pairs are 3 and 4, and 7 and 8. Say those back.

step_4_feel_check.name: Feel Check
step_4_feel_check.description: Audiation test. Student hears pairs and identifies which feels together. This is internal evidence, never a student-facing score.
step_4_feel_check.student_facing_intro: Close your eyes. I will play two pairs. Tell me which pair felt closer — first or second.

step_5_name_it.name: Name It
step_5_name_it.description: Music-world names are revealed only after the student hears, says, and feels skip/together.
step_5_name_it.motesart_reveal: You already know skip and together. Now here are the music-world names. The music-world name for skip is whole step. The music-world name for together is half step. You already know the music. Now you know what musicians call it.
step_5_name_it.child_version: You know skip. Musicians call that a whole step. You know together. Musicians call that a half step.
step_5_name_it.teen_version: Music-world names: skip is whole step. Together is half step. Same moves, official names.
step_5_name_it.adult_version: Music-world names: skip equals whole step. Together equals half step. Same relationship, technical vocabulary.
step_5_name_it.visual: Skip → Whole step. Together → Half step. 3-4 and 7-8 remain highlighted as together pairs.

locked_terms.reveal_trigger: after step_3 and step_4 both completed

step_6_quiz_it.name: Quiz It
step_6_quiz_it.description: Execution questions. Motesart is absent during quiz questions per Article XII. Feedback uses Motesart words first.

questions.motesart_correct: Yes. 3 and 4, and 7 and 8 are together.
questions.motesart_wrong: Close — get specific. The together pairs are 3 and 4, and 7 and 8.

questions.prompt: Between 3 and 4, do we skip or stay together?
questions.motesart_wrong: 3 and 4 are together. They are holding hands.

questions.prompt: Between 1 and 2, do we skip or stay together?
questions.motesart_correct: Skip. There is a note between.
questions.motesart_wrong: Between 1 and 2, there is space. That is skip.

questions.prompt: Build the pattern using skip and together.
acceptable_answers: skip skip together skip skip skip together
skip, skip, together, skip, skip, skip, together
questions.motesart_correct: That is the pattern. Skip, skip, together, skip, skip, skip, together.
questions.motesart_wrong: Take your time. The close spots are 3 and 4, and 7 and 8.

questions.prompt: What is the music-world name for together?
questions.motesart_correct: Half step. You already knew it as together.
questions.motesart_wrong: The music-world name for together is half step.

questions.prompt: What is the music-world name for skip?
questions.motesart_correct: Whole step. Same move as skip.
questions.motesart_wrong: The music-world name for skip is whole step.

questions.prompt: In your own words — what is the difference between a skip and together?
questions.motesart_correct: That is ownership. You can explain the difference, not just repeat the words.
questions.motesart_wrong: You've got the idea. Now make it exact: skip has space, together has no space.

step_7_explain_it.name: Explain It
step_7_explain_it.description: Ownership gate. Student explains skip and together in their own words.

step_8_homework.name: Homework
step_8_homework.description: Launch FindTheNote Academic mode for find_together when wired.

step_9_evidence_complete.name: Evidence Complete
step_9_evidence_complete.description: Internal gate evidence summary. Student sees tier language, not percentages.
step_9_evidence_complete.complete_message: Skip and together are locked. Now the family pattern can make sense.

wyl_interventions.description: WYL fires after mistake detection, from mistake codes rather than fixed student labels.

visual.child: Show numbers 1 through 8. Put a small bridge over 3 and 4, and 7 and 8. Caption: 'These are holding hands.'
visual.teen: Show the numbered pattern only. 3-4 and 7-8 are highlighted as together. All other pairs show a gap.
visual.adult: Show interval map by number position: together at 3-4 and 7-8, skip everywhere else.
visual.interaction: Student taps the together pairs on the number map.

auditory.child: Play a skip, then a together pair. Motesart says: 'Hear the space? Now hear the close one?'
auditory.teen: Play two pairs and ask which one sounds closer. Repeat until together is recognized.
auditory.adult: Play whole-step and half-step pairs without naming them first. Student identifies skip or together by sound.
auditory.interaction: Student answers skip or together after each pair.

kinesthetic.child: Student moves a finger from 3 to 4 without lifting far, then from 1 to 2 with a skip space shown.
kinesthetic.teen: Student traces the pattern: skip, skip, together, skip, skip, skip, together.
kinesthetic.adult: Student maps finger movement across the numbered pattern and labels the two close moves.
kinesthetic.interaction: Student performs or describes the motion for 3-4 and 7-8.

readwrite.child: Fill in: 'Skip means there is a __ between. Together means no __ between.'
readwrite.teen: Write the rule: skip = space between; together = no space between. Then name the together pairs.
readwrite.adult: Define skip and together in one sentence each, then translate them to whole step and half step.
readwrite.interaction: Student completes rule statements and identifies 3-4 and 7-8.

categories.description: Student places together pairs at wrong positions
categories.trigger: G1_Q1 or G1_Q2 answer misses 3-4 or 7-8
categories.next_action: trigger WYL visual — numbered map with 3-4 and 7-8 highlighted

categories.description: Student reverses skip and together definitions
categories.trigger: student says skip means no note between or together means a note between
categories.next_action: trigger WYL auditory or kinesthetic — compare space vs no space

categories.description: Student uses letter names C D E F instead of numbers
categories.trigger: answer relies only on letter names without identifying number positions
categories.next_action: redirect to numbers first: 3 and 4, 7 and 8

categories.description: Student can recite but cannot explain the relationship
categories.trigger: G1_Q4 passes but ownership explanation is vague or missing one definition
categories.next_action: trigger WYL readwrite — define skip and together separately

categories.description: Student passes Q1-Q6 but fails ownership
categories.trigger: execution questions pass but G1_Q7 ownership explanation fails
categories.next_action: flag as execution_only — ownership gate not passed — require retry or teacher review

mastery_rule.execution_definition: Student answers G1_Q1 through G1_Q6 with score >= 0.85
mastery_rule.ownership_definition: Student explains skip and together in own words with at least one acceptable signal for each concept

not_ready.motesart_response: Let's back up. We need more time here before we move on.

developing.motesart_response: You're getting there. Let's try that again.

almost_owned.motesart_response: You almost had it. One more pass and it'll stick.

mastered.motesart_response: That is locked. You know skip and together.

homework_game.prompt: Is this a skip or together?
homework_game.description: Student hears two notes played together. They identify whether the pair is a skip or together. Level 1, one octave, C major.
